summary.text: A 27-year-old apparently healthy Sri Lankan woman, a teacher with no significant past medical or surgical history, conceived three months after stopping the oral contraceptive pill. Urine was positive for human chorionic gonadotropin, and an antenatal visit found her clinical examination, full blood count and urine report normal. She had not complained of breathlessness, chest tightness, syncope or palpitation, and history did not reveal chest pain, and there was no family history of sudden death or ARVC/D.

At about the 11th week of amenorrhea she was found collapsed in the toilet of her house and was pronounced dead on admission to hospital. A medico-legal autopsy found a moderately dilated right ventricle with 1-3 mm wall thickness and epicardial fat 4-5 mm thick infiltrating the myocardium, with an intrauterine foetus, while other cardiac structures were macroscopically normal and no other macroscopic abnormalities were detected.

Histology showed significant replacement of right ventricular myocardium with fibro-fatty tissue on H&E and Masson trichrome stains, without inflammatory cells, and the other cardiac structures and organs were normal; microbiological and toxicological screening were negative. The cause of death was given as ARVC/D in the first trimester of pregnancy and the circumstance was concluded as natural. Genetic studies were not done, and relatives have been advised regarding diagnostic availability.
